title: WinSCP saved sessions file
whyItMatters: When WinSCP is set to store its configuration in an INI file, saved sessions and stored passwords sit in it. A stranger could reconnect to the same servers.
source: WinSCP documentation, Configuration: storage can be an INI file, by default WinSCP.ini next to the executable or in the user profile - https://winscp.net/eng/docs/config
notes: Only exists when INI storage was chosen. By default WinSCP keeps sessions in the HKCU registry, which cannot be expressed as a path rule, so registry-stored sessions are not covered here. Stored passwords may be obfuscated, not encrypted.

cleanup.exportFirst: Open WinSCP and note the host names you still need, since the saved sessions are removed with the file.
cleanup.signOut: Change the passwords of the server accounts this PC connected to, because stored copies keep working after the file is gone.
steps: Change the server account passwords at the hosting provider.
Uninstall WinSCP from Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
Delete the file named in the plan if it is still there.
cleanup.risk: Removes saved WinSCP sessions and passwords from this PC. Server accounts stay usable until their passwords are changed.
